title: Post-launch review: overload protection impact (incidents, p99 latency, support tickets) + next iteration plan
creator: Talia Benson
body:
Goal
Compare reliability + performance outcomes pre/post overload protection rollout for Hosted API, and decide next iteration scope.

Context
We enabled layered overload protection (edge admission control + routing breaker evaluation + runtime bounded queues/shed points) behind feature flags, then rolled out starting with us-east canary and expanded globally. We also updated SLO accounting to separate overload-protected errors from internal failures.

Review window
- Pre-period: 2025-12-01 → 2026-01-04 (5 weeks)
- Post-period: 2026-01-07 → 2026-02-16 (6 weeks)

Data sources (links)
- Grafana: Overload Protection dashboard (breaker transitions, shed rate, queue depth, latency): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/overload-protection
- SLO toolkit report (Hosted API): https://slo.redwoodinference.com/services/hosted-api
- Incident bot snapshots for overload-labeled incidents: https://incident-bot.redwoodinference.com/overload-snapshots
- Support tickets (SUP): SUP-3921, SUP-3928, SUP-3955, SUP-3961, SUP-3974
- Rollout notes: ENG-4834, game day findings: ENG-4835

What we measured
1) Incidents
- Sev1/Sev2 incidents where primary contributor was overload (GPU pool saturation, queue blowups, regional brownouts).
- Secondary: number of “cascade” patterns (control plane latency leading to widespread request timeouts).

2) Latency
- p99 end-to-end latency for top 10 routes/models in Hosted.
- Split by: streaming vs non-streaming, region, tier.
- Special attention to tail behavior during spikes (p99 and “p99 of p99” during peak 5-minute windows).

3) Customer-facing errors + retries
- Rate of 429/503 with Redwood overload codes vs generic 5xx timeouts.
- Presence of Retry-After and consistency across REST and OpenAI-compat.
- Evidence of retry storms / client retry loops (429 amplification).

4) Support volume + sentiment
- Ticket volume tagged as “timeouts/503/429 under load” and “retry guidance”
- Common customer misunderstandings (billing, Retry-After interpretation, streaming disconnect behavior).

Results (summary)
Incidents
- Pre: 4 overload-driven Sev2, 2 overload-driven Sev1 (6 total); 3 showed cascade into control plane latency + elevated 5xx.
- Post: 1 overload-driven Sev2, 0 Sev1 (1 total); 0 cascades observed.
- Net: -83% overload-driven Sev1/Sev2 incidents.
Notes:
- The remaining Sev2 (2026-02-03) was caused by a capacity signal delay in eu-west leading to breaker not opening quickly enough; mitigated by temporarily lowering thresholds + region shift.

Latency (Hosted API)
- Baseline p99 (all traffic, all regions): improved ~8–12% depending on route due to reduced queue blowups.
- Peak-window p99 (top 5% busiest 5-minute windows): improved ~25–35% on affected models.
- Worst-case tail: materially reduced; we no longer see multi-minute p99 collapse during step-function traffic.
Caveats:
- Slight increase in p50/p90 on one long-context route in us-west during initial queue bounding rollout (since resolved via tuning + avoiding overly aggressive early shed at prefill). See ENG-4840 + runtime tuning follow-ups.

Error mix + customer experience
- Pre:
  - Elevated ambiguous failures under overload: mix of 500/502/503, frequent client-perceived timeouts.
  - Retry behavior inconsistent; some requests retried immediately (client-side) causing amplification.
- Post:
  - Overload manifests primarily as 429 (tier admission control) or 503 (capacity/breaker open), with Redwood overload codes and consistent Retry-After.
  - Internal 5xx during overload windows down significantly; timeouts reduced.
  - We did see a short-term increase in 429 complaints after enabling in us-east (SUP-3974) traced to a client retry loop without jitter; Support now has a standard response and SDK helpers exist.

Support tickets
- Pre-period: 11 tickets/month (avg) referencing timeouts/503 under spikes; common request was “clearer errors + how long to wait”.
- Post-period: 6 tickets/month (avg) referencing overload; topics shifted from “why am I timing out?” to “how should I interpret Retry-After / does this count as usage?”.
- Notable tickets:
  - SUP-3928: resolved with docs + consistent error payload guidance.
  - SUP-3961: clarified billing behavior + recommended backoff; added to FAQ.
  - SUP-3974: mitigation was client-side jitter + capped retries; follow-up to improve SDK defaults.

SLO / Error budget accounting
- With the new SLO toolkit change, we can separately track:
  - Internal errors (incident-worthy, page)
  - Overload-protected errors (expected under extreme load; alert but do not page by default)
- Outcome: paging noise decreased without masking true regressions. Oncall reports fewer “false Sev2s” during known spikes.

Decision / Next iteration (agreed)
Proceed with Iteration 2 scoped to the following:
1) Streaming resilience under overload (P0 for next cycle)
- Add clearer semantics for mid-stream disconnect vs shed-before-start.
- Ensure consistent error codes and tracing for streaming termination cases.
- Partner with Runtime to avoid shedding after decode starts when possible; if unavoidable, surface explicit reason.

2) Faster + safer breaker response to signal delays (P1)
- Improve capacity signal freshness/propagation for eu-west (and document SLOs for signal latency).
- Add a “failsafe open” mode when signals are stale beyond threshold to prevent queue spiral.

3) SDK defaults for retry/backoff (P1)
- Ship safe-by-default capped retries + jitter helpers in Python/TS/Go SDKs and recommend enabling.
- Update docs to explicitly warn about synchronized retries and infinite loops.

4) Observability hygiene (P2)
- Reduce high-cardinality labels and standardize overload reason tags across gateway/routing/runtime.
- Add a consolidated “customer impact view”: shed rate + top affected models/regions + estimated rejected QPS.

Out of scope / not now
- Major scheduler redesign.
- Customer-specific bespoke overload logic beyond existing policy primitives.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Produce a written summary with pre/post metrics (incidents, latency, support).
- [x] Confirm with SRE oncall what changed in paging and whether it introduced blind spots.
- [x] Capture top 3 follow-up investments and turn into new Linear tickets with owners.
- [x] PM sign-off (Hosted API) on customer-facing learnings + docs follow-ups.

Follow-ups created
- ENG-4922: Streaming overload semantics + runtime shed constraints
- ENG-4923: Capacity signal freshness SLO + stale-signal failsafe
- ENG-4924: SDK retry defaults + jitter helper rollout
- ENG-4925: Overload dashboard “customer impact view” panel

Risks / open questions (recorded)
- Risk: If we tune too aggressively toward shedding early, some customers may see more 429/503 even when we could have served them with slightly higher latency. Need to monitor “served tokens/sec” vs “shed rate” tradeoff per tier.
- Question: Should we treat 503 (breaker open) differently for Dedicated vs Hosted in shared docs to avoid confusion? (PM + Dedicated alignment needed.)

Appendix: notable observations
- Breaker flapping hotfix (PR-18519) materially improved stability; post-period numbers exclude the initial 24h where flapping caused noisy transitions.
- Retry-After values: 5–15s is working better than 1–2s; reduces herd effects without making recovery feel too slow. Continue to validate per region.
comments: 2026-01-16 (Talia Benson): Creating post-launch review ticket per program deliverable. Please use consistent pre/post windows and include support ticket summary + SLO accounting changes.

2026-01-23 (Tomáš Novák): Pulled incident stats from #incidents + oncall reports. Preliminary: overload-driven Sev1/2 down significantly post rollout; will quantify and cross-check with SLO toolkit views.

2026-01-30 (Aisha Bello): Added dashboards for breaker transitions + shed rate by (model, region, tier). Note: label cardinality is trending high for route; please avoid adding customer_id anywhere in metrics.

2026-02-04 (Rafael Mendes): +1 on calling out the remaining Sev2 in eu-west as a signal freshness issue. We should track signal propagation latency as a first-class metric and consider stale-signal fail-open.

2026-02-11 (Nikhil Sharma): Please include customer-facing learnings: fewer ambiguous 5xx, more actionable 429/503 w/ Retry-After, and the one sharp edge (clients retrying too aggressively). Docs and SDKs should lean into safe defaults.
2026-02-18 (Tomáš Novák): Draft results posted in body. Key decision proposal: focus next iteration on streaming semantics + signal freshness + SDK retry defaults. Will close after PM sign-off.
2026-02-21 (Henry Cho): Reviewed summary; aligns with PM view. Biggest gap is streaming disconnect messaging—customers still interpret it as instability. Approved to close with follow-up tickets.
